body.statement: Let \(m=3\), \(\Omega=\{1,2,3\}\), \(\pi(i)=1/3\), and \(L=\{(1,1),(2,2),(3,3),(1,2),(2,3),(3,1)\}\). At \(\alpha=2/3\), take \(q=1\), \(w_1=1\), and \(s^1(1)>s^1(2)>s^1(3)\). The legal nonpartition kernel \[K=\begin{pmatrix}2/3&1/3&0\\0&2/3&1/3\\1/3&0&2/3\end{pmatrix}\] satisfies \(d_K(A)\geq\pi(A)\) for every nonempty \(A\subseteq\Omega\) and has \(\operatorname{Pow}(K)=2/3\). Every member of \(\mathcal{P}_L\) has singleton cells, hence \(K(x,y)=\mathbf{1}\{x=y\}\) and power zero. Consequently \(K\) is globally catalogue-power optimal and \(\Delta_{\mathrm{part}}=2/3\).
body.justification: The smallest directed-cycle fiber turns enlargement of the valid design class into a certified, strictly positive operational power gain.
body.gap: Partition and biclique methods cannot use any off-diagonal comparison on this asymmetric support, while the valid cyclic row kernel uses all three directed comparisons.
body.consumer: The Cai weather-insurance presolve can use this instance as a unit test before seeking a strict partition gap on an empirical legal fiber.
